headline: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
name: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
description: This investigation addresses critical deficiencies in Indonesian Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits (IMDGNP) peatland boundary estimations through systematic verification of peat soil distributions in Pontianak City, West Kalimantan Province. Preliminary IMDGNP cartographic products at 1:250,000 scale identified four administrative districts containing peatland formations totaling 23.8649 km² , exhibiting documented accuracy limitations requiring comprehensive field validation. The research methodology integrated systematic field reconnaissance encompassing 614 observation points at 250-meter intervals, laboratory classification testing of 68 undisturbed soil specimens following ASTM D4427 (organic content > 75% threshold) and ASTM D2974 (ash content < 25% threshold) standardized procedures, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) spatial analysis for refined boundary demarcation at 1:50,000 scale. Results demonstrate that peat soil formations are confined to only two districts —Southeast Pontianak (5.798 km² , 35.95% of district area) and North Pontianak (17.320 km² , 42.14% of district area) —contrary to preliminary four -district estimations. Contrary to the preliminary four -district IMDGNP estimate of 23.8649 km² , verified peatland formations total 23.118 km² and are confined to only two districts. Within North Pontianak District specifically, the verified extent (17.320 km² ) exceeds the preliminary district-level IMDGNP estimate (12.7683 km² ) by 35.76%, while Pontianak City and East Pontianak districts contain organic soils rather than peat formations. The updated demarcation mapping incorporates peat layer depth information within a comprehensive geospatial database suitable for infrastructure planning , foundation design optimization, and building conserv ation, thereby supporting evidence -based urban development and environmental management aligned with tropical peatland ecosystem governance principles.

hasPart.name: 1. INTRODUCTION
hasPart.description: This section introduces the study addressing critical deficiencies in Indonesian peatland boundary estimations. It outlines the significance of accurate peatland mapping and sets the research objectives for Pontianak City, West Kalimantan Province.

hasPart.name: 2. RESEARCH METHODS
hasPart.description: This section details the methodological framework used to verify peat soil distribution. It describes the study area, field investigation, sampling strategies, laboratory testing, and geographic information system analysis.

hasPart.name: 2.1 Study area
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the geographical characteristics and administrative districts of the study area in Pontianak City, West Kalimantan. It provides context on the environmental setting and targeted zones for peatland verification.

hasPart.name: 2.2 Field investigation and data collection
hasPart.description: This subsection explains the procedures and protocols followed during the field investigations. It covers the collection of primary data and observations necessary for assessing peat soil distribution.

hasPart.name: 2.3 Sampling strategy
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the strategic approach utilized for selecting soil sampling sites. It establishes the criteria and framework to ensure representative data acquisition across the study zones.

hasPart.name: 2.3.1 Sampling location determination
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the specific criteria and methods used to pinpoint exact geographic locations for soil sampling. It ensures spatial coverage and accuracy in data gathering.

hasPart.name: 2.3.2 Field sampling procedures
hasPart.description: This subsection details the step-by-step procedures executed in the field to collect soil samples. It ensures consistency and adherence to scientific standards during sample extraction.

hasPart.name: 2.4 Organic content and ash content testing
hasPart.description: This subsection explains the laboratory testing methods used to determine organic matter and ash content in the collected soil samples. These tests help classify and verify the peat composition.

hasPart.name: 2.5 Geographic Information System analysis
hasPart.description: This subsection provides an overview of the geospatial techniques applied to process spatial data. It sets the foundation for mapping and evaluating the extent of peatland areas.

hasPart.name: 2.5.1 Spatial data components
hasPart.description: This subsection identifies the various spatial datasets and layers incorporated into the analysis. It details the inputs required for accurate geographic modeling.

hasPart.name: 2.5.2 Geographic Information System development and processing
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the workflow for building and processing the GIS database. It highlights how spatial analysis tools were utilized to evaluate peatland boundaries.

hasPart.name: 2.6 Research flowchart
hasPart.description: This subsection presents a comprehensive flowchart summarizing the entire research methodology. It visually maps out the sequential steps from data collection to final analysis.

hasPart.name: 3. RESULTS AND ANALYSIS
hasPart.description: This section presents the findings obtained from field investigations and laboratory testing. It includes detailed land use classifications, laboratory results, and geospatial mapping evaluations.

hasPart.name: 3.1 Field investigation results
hasPart.description: This subsection details the primary findings gathered directly from the field surveys. It highlights initial observations regarding peatland presence and site conditions.

hasPart.name: 3.1.1 Preliminary peatland distribution from Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits map
hasPart.description: This subsection reviews the initial peatland distribution estimates derived from official permit delay maps. It establishes a baseline for comparison against verified ground data.

hasPart.name: 3.1.2 Land use classification results
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the categorization of different land use types observed within the study area. It categorizes how verified peatlands are currently utilized.

hasPart.name: 3.2 Laboratory classification results
hasPart.description: This subsection summarizes the outcomes of laboratory soil analyses. It provides quantitative metrics regarding the physical and chemical properties of the samples.

hasPart.name: 3.2.1 Organic content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection presents the specific organic content percentages measured in the laboratory tests. These values confirm the presence and grade of organic soils.

hasPart.name: 3.2.2 Ash content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection details the ash content findings from the soil samples. It provides crucial indicators for differentiating peat soil layers and mineral soils.

hasPart.name: 3.3 Data analysis and evaluation
hasPart.description: This subsection synthesizes the field and laboratory data to evaluate overall peatland characteristics. It bridges raw measurements with practical environmental assessments.

hasPart.name: 3.3.1 Land use assessment in verified peatland areas
hasPart.description: This subsection evaluates the specific human activities and land covers present on verified peatlands. It assesses potential environmental pressures and management needs.

hasPart.name: 3.3.2 Peatland demarcation refinement and boundary
hasPart.description: This subsection discusses the adjustments made to official peatland boundaries based on empirical data. It refines mapping accuracy for better spatial planning.

hasPart.name: 3.3.3 Peat soil layer depth classification
hasPart.description: This subsection classifies the measured depths of the peat soil layers across various study sites. It provides a vertical dimension to the spatial distribution analysis.

hasPart.name: Results
hasPart.description: This section consolidates key analytical outcomes regarding depth classifications and soil characteristics. It provides intermediary findings prior to full geospatial integration.

hasPart.name: 3.4 Geospatial mapping and GIS assessment
hasPart.description: This subsection details the advanced GIS assessments and spatial modeling performed. It translates field and lab discoveries into comprehensive digital maps.

hasPart.name: 3.4.1 Comparative analysis: IMDGNP vs verified boundaries
hasPart.description: This subsection compares official permit map boundaries with the newly verified empirical boundaries. It highlights discrepancies and improvements in mapping precision.

hasPart.name: 3.4.2 Final demarcation mapping products
hasPart.description: This subsection presents the final cartographic outputs resulting from the study. It delivers updated spatial products designed to guide future environmental management.

hasPart.name: 4. CONCLUSION
hasPart.description: This section summarizes the primary findings and contributions of the research. It emphasizes the importance of accurate geospatial verification for sustainable peatland governance.
